 Order
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

2. This petition has been filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short,
'Cr.P.C.') seeking quashing of FIR No.126/2023 registered at Police Station: Sector 23, Dwarka, New Delhi for offence under Sections 498A/406/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short, 'IPC'),
along with all other proceedings arising therefrom, on the basis of a settlement.
3. Issue notice.
4. Notice is accepted by Mr.Shoaib Haider, the learned APP and This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 01/06/2024 at 01:20:55 by Mr.Manjeet Godara, Advocate on behalf of the respondent no.2.
5.

The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the subject FIR was an offshoot of the Akshansh Agarwal & Ors vs State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100772204/
1 matrimonial discord between the parties, that is, the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2.
6.

entities.text: Akshansh Agarwal & Ors vs State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He submits that the parties have amicably settled their inter se disputes and have entered into a Memorandum of Understanding / settlement dated 23.03.2024.

7. Pursuant to the abovementioned settlement, the parties have obtained divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 20.05.2024 passed by the learned Judge, Family Courts, Dwarka,
Delhi.

8. The Respondent no.2, who appears in Court through virtual mode and has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer (IO), reaffirms the above-mentioned settlement and states that she has settled all the disputes with the petitioners out of her own free will and without any coercion.
She submits that she has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
9. The petitioners have handed over a Demand Draft of Rs.12,50,000/- to the learned counsel for the respondent no.2 in terms of the settlement.
10. I have perused the contents of the FIR and also the Settlement between the parties.

11. Keeping in view the fact that the disputes between the parties arose out of a matrimonial relationship, and now the same have been amicably settled, a decree of divorce has also been passed by the learned Family Court pursuant to the settlement and also looking into
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 01/06/2024 at 01:20:55 the nature of the allegations made in the complaint, in my opinion, no useful purpose would be served in keeping the FIR alive.
In fact, it would rather create further acrimony between the parties and will be an unnecessary burden on the State Exchequer.

12. Guided by the principles enunciated by the Supreme Court in its judgments in Jitendra Raghuvanshi v. Babita Raghuvanshi, (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303; Parbatbhai Aahir @ Parbatbhai Bhimsinbhai Karmur & Ors. v. State of Gujarat & Ors.
